claim: The Reissner fiber is an extracellular thread conserved in vertebrates that is contained in the cerebrospinal fluid.
source: The cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) contains an extracellular thread conserved in vertebrates, the Reissner fiber, which controls body axis morphogenesis in the zebrafish embryo.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and is supported by citations to prior work on the Reissner fiber.

claim: The Reissner fiber controls body axis morphogenesis in the zebrafish embryo.
source: The cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) contains an extracellular thread conserved in vertebrates, the Reissner fiber, which controls body axis morphogenesis in the zebrafish embryo.
evidence: This claim is stated in the abstract and is supported by the authors' previous work (Cantaut-Belarif et al., 2018).

claim: The Reissner fiber is required in vivo for the expression of urp2, a neuropeptide expressed in CSF-contacting neurons.
source: First, we show that the Reissner fiber is required in vivo for the expression of urp2, a neuropeptide expressed in CSF-cNs.
evidence: This is demonstrated through transcriptomic analysis and qRT-PCR experiments showing decreased urp2 expression in scospondin mutants lacking the Reissner fiber.

claim: The Reissner fiber is required for embryonic calcium transients in spinal neurons contacting the CSF.
source: We show that the Reissner fiber is also required for embryonic calcium transients in these spinal neurons.
evidence: This is demonstrated through in vivo calcium imaging showing reduced calcium activity in ventral CSF-cNs of scospondin mutants.

claim: Local adrenergic activation can substitute for the Reissner fiber-signaling pathway to CSF-cNs and rescue body axis morphogenesis.
source: Finally, we study how local adrenergic activation can substitute for the Reissner fiber-signaling pathway to CSF-cNs and rescue body axis morphogenesis.
evidence: This is demonstrated through experiments showing that epinephrine and norepinephrine injections can restore calcium signaling, urp2 expression, and body axis straightness in scospondin mutants.

claim: The Reissner fiber acts on CSF-cNs and thereby contributes to establish body axis morphogenesis.
source: Our results show that the Reissner fiber acts on CSF-cNs and thereby contributes to establish body axis morphogenesis, and suggest it does so by controlling the availability of a chemical signal in the CSF.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the combined results of transcriptomic analysis, calcium imaging, and pharmacological rescue experiments.

claim: The Reissner fiber controls the availability of a chemical signal in the CSF.
source: Our results show that the Reissner fiber acts on CSF-cNs and thereby contributes to establish body axis morphogenesis, and suggest it does so by controlling the availability of a chemical signal in the CSF.
evidence: This is suggested based on the ability of monoamines to rescue the phenotype and the detection of norepinephrine associated with the Reissner fiber.

claim: The CSF contains many signals important for cell differentiation.
source: It has recently emerged that the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) contains many signals important for cell differentiation, and is an important route for the control of morphogenesis (Fame and Lehtinen, 2020).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Fame and Lehtinen, 2020.

claim: The CSF is an important route for the control of morphogenesis.
source: It has recently emerged that the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) contains many signals important for cell differentiation, and is an important route for the control of morphogenesis (Fame and Lehtinen, 2020).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Fame and Lehtinen, 2020.

claim: The CSF is a complex liquid filling the central nervous system cavities containing a set of diffusible signaling cues guiding neurogenesis.
source: The CSF is a complex liquid filling the central nervous system cavities containing a set of diffusible signaling cues guiding neurogenesis (Lehtinen et al., 2011) and brain morphology in a tissue autonomous manner (Kaiser et al., 2019; Langford et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Lehtinen et al., 2011; Kaiser et al., 2019; Langford et al., 2020.

claim: The CSF circulation is in part generated by the coordinated movement of cilia projecting to the lumen of brain ventricles and central canal of the spinal cord.
source: The CSF circulation is in part generated by the coordinated movement of cilia projecting to the lumen of brain ventricles and central canal of the spinal cord (Faubel et al., 2016; Hagenlocher et al., 2013; Olstad et al., 2019; Sternberg et al., 2018; Thouvenin et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to studies on cilia and CSF circulation.

claim: Disruption of cilia motility in zebrafish induces a typical phenotype consisting in a downward curvature of the posterior axis of the embryo.
source: Indeed, disruption of cilia motility in this species has been long known to induce a typical phenotype consisting in a downward curvature of the posterior axis of the embryo (Brand et al., 1996; Jaffe et al., 2016; Kramer-Zucker et al., 2005; Sullivan-Brown et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to studies on cilia-defective mutants.

claim: The curled-down phenotype in cilia-defective mutants has been linked to a role of the CSF in body axis curvature establishment and maintenance downstream of cilia function.
source: This phenotype has recently been linked to a role of the CSF in body axis curvature establishment and maintenance downstream of cilia function (Cantaut-Belarif et al., 2018; Grimes et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Cantaut-Belarif et al., 2018 and Grimes et al., 2016.

claim: The Reissner fiber is important for axis morphogenesis in the zebrafish embryo.
source: We previously showed that the Reissner fiber (RF), a component of the CSF, is important for axis morphogenesis in the zebrafish embryo (Cantaut-Belarif et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by the authors' previous work cited as Cantaut-Belarif et al., 2018.

claim: The Reissner fiber is an acellular proteinous thread bathing in the brain and spinal cord cavities early in development.
source: The Reissner fiber (Reissner, 1860) is an acellular proteinous thread bathing in the brain and spinal cord cavities early in development (Troutwine et al., 2020), formed by the aggregation of the SCO-spondin glycoprotein, secreted into the CSF by the subcommissural organ and the floor plate (Lehmann and Naumann, 2005; Meiniel et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Reissner, 1860; Troutwine et al., 2020; Lehmann and Naumann, 2005; Meiniel et al., 2008.

claim: The Reissner fiber is formed by the aggregation of the SCO-spondin glycoprotein.
source: The Reissner fiber (Reissner, 1860) is an acellular proteinous thread bathing in the brain and spinal cord cavities early in development (Troutwine et al., 2020), formed by the aggregation of the SCO-spondin glycoprotein, secreted into the CSF by the subcommissural organ and the floor plate (Lehmann and Naumann, 2005; Meiniel et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Lehmann and Naumann, 2005; Meiniel et al., 2008.

claim: SCO-spondin is secreted into the CSF by the subcommissural organ and the floor plate.
source: The Reissner fiber (Reissner, 1860) is an acellular proteinous thread bathing in the brain and spinal cord cavities early in development (Troutwine et al., 2020), formed by the aggregation of the SCO-spondin glycoprotein, secreted into the CSF by the subcommissural organ and the floor plate (Lehmann and Naumann, 2005; Meiniel et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Lehmann and Naumann, 2005; Meiniel et al., 2008.

claim: The Reissner fiber fails to assemble in cilia-defective mutants.
source: This fiber fails to assemble in cilia-defective mutants, and scospondin mutant embryos lacking the Reissner fiber exhibit a curled-down axis despite exhibiting normal cilia motility and CSF flow (Cantaut-Belarif et al., 2018; Rose et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Cantaut-Belarif et al., 2018 and Rose et al., 2020.

claim: Scospondin mutant embryos lacking the Reissner fiber exhibit a curled-down axis despite exhibiting normal cilia motility and CSF flow.
source: This fiber fails to assemble in cilia-defective mutants, and scospondin mutant embryos lacking the Reissner fiber exhibit a curled-down axis despite exhibiting normal cilia motility and CSF flow (Cantaut-Belarif et al., 2018; Rose et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Cantaut-Belarif et al., 2018 and Rose et al., 2020.

claim: The absence of the Reissner fiber causes a curled-down phenotype, including in cilia-defective mutants.
source: These observations suggest that the fiber itself plays a role in the control of body axis morphogenesis in the embryo, and that its absence causes a curled-down phenotype, including in cilia-defective mutants.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that both cilia-defective mutants and scospondin mutants exhibit the same phenotype.

claim: Bath applications of monoamines can restore a straight axis in embryos with a curled-down phenotype.
source: Recent studies suggest that bath applications of monoamines can restore a straight axis in embryos with a curled-down phenotype (Lu et al., 2020; Zhang et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Lu et al., 2020 and Zhang et al., 2018.

claim: Radiolabeled norepinephrine can bind the Reissner fiber in the CSF of rats.
source: Radiolabeled norepinephrine can bind the Reissner fiber in the CSF of rats (Caprile et al., 2003) and frogs (Diederen et al., 1983).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Caprile et al., 2003 and Diederen et al., 1983.

claim: Radiolabeled norepinephrine can bind the Reissner fiber in the CSF of frogs.
source: Radiolabeled norepinephrine can bind the Reissner fiber in the CSF of rats (Caprile et al., 2003) and frogs (Diederen et al., 1983).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Caprile et al., 2003 and Diederen et al., 1983.

claim: Monoamines influence many neurophysiological processes in the adult such as sleep control.
source: Monoamines are widespread neurotransmitters and neuromodulators that include epinephrine and norepinephrine, and influence many neurophysiological processes in the adult such as sleep control (Singh et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Singh et al., 2015.

claim: The signal controlling axis morphogenesis downstream of CSF flow has been associated with changes in the expression of Urp1 and Urp2 peptides.
source: In addition, the signal controlling axis morphogenesis downstream of CSF flow has been associated with changes in the expression of Urp1 and Urp2 peptides (Lu et al., 2020; Zhang et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Lu et al., 2020 and Zhang et al., 2018.

claim: Urp1 and Urp2 peptides belong to a family of neuropeptides similar to Urotensin-II.
source: These peptides belong to a family of neuropeptides similar to Urotensin-II previously shown to mediate endocrine, cardiac, and neurophysiological functions (Vaudry et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Vaudry et al., 2015.

claim: In the zebrafish embryo, urp1 and urp2 are expressed along the antero-posterior axis of the neural tube in a subset of spinal sensory neurons called CSF-contacting neurons.
source: In the zebrafish embryo, urp1 and urp2 are expressed along the antero-posterior axis of the neural tube in a subset of spinal sensory neurons (Quan et al., 2015) called CSF-contacting neurons (CSF-cNs).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Quan et al., 2015.

claim: CSF-cNs extend into the CSF a microvilliated apical extension that starts differentiating in the embryo and becomes fully mature in the larva to tune the mechanosensory responses of CSF-cNs upon tail bending.
source: CSF-cNs extend into the CSF a microvilliated apical extension that starts differentiating in the embryo and becomes fully mature in the larva to tune the mechanosensory responses of CSF-cNs upon tail bending (Desban et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Desban et al., 2019.

claim: CSF-cNs form two populations of different developmental origins that are located ventrally and dorso-laterally relative to the central canal of the zebrafish spinal cord.
source: These conserved interoceptive neurons form two populations of different developmental origins that are located ventrally and dorso-laterally relative to the central canal of the zebrafish spinal cord (Djenoune et al., 2017; Park et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Djenoune et al., 2017 and Park et al., 2004.

claim: At the embryonic stage, undifferentiated CSF-cNs that are located ventrally in the neural tube are the only ones expressing Urp neuropeptides and exhibiting spontaneous calcium transients at rest.
source: At the embryonic stage, undifferentiated CSF-cNs that are located ventrally in the neural tube are the only ones expressing Urp neuropeptides and exhibiting spontaneous calcium transients at rest (Sternberg et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Sternberg et al., 2018.

claim: The Reissner fiber was shown to be required in the larva for the mechanosensory function leading to intracellular calcium increase in differentiated CSF-cNs.
source: Recently, the Reissner fiber was shown to be required in the larva for the mechanosensory function leading to intracellular calcium increase in differentiated CSF-cNs (Orts-Del'Immagine et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Orts-Del'Immagine et al., 2020.

claim: The scospondinicm13 null allele leads to a dual loss of the fiber in the central canal and of the SCO-spondin protein detection in secretory structures.
source: While the scospondinicm13 null allele leads to a dual loss of the fiber in the central canal and of the SCO-spondin protein detection in secretory structures, the scospondinicm15 hypomorphic allele retains protein expression but solely precludes the Reissner fiber formation (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and illustrated in Figure 1A.

claim: The scospondinicm15 hypomorphic allele retains protein expression but solely precludes the Reissner fiber formation.
source: While the scospondinicm13 null allele leads to a dual loss of the fiber in the central canal and of the SCO-spondin protein detection in secretory structures, the scospondinicm15 hypomorphic allele retains protein expression but solely precludes the Reissner fiber formation (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and illustrated in Figure 1A.

claim: Both scospondinicm13 and scospondinicm15 homozygous mutants lack the Reissner fiber and exhibit a typical curled-down phenotype.
source: Both homozygous mutants lack the Reissner fiber and exhibit a typical curled-down phenotype, which arises from 28 to 30 hr post-fertilization (hpf) onwards and was undetectable beforehand (Cantaut-Belarif et al., 2018, Figure 1A, Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 1A and Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: The curled-down phenotype in scospondin mutants arises from 28 to 30 hr post-fertilization (hpf) onwards and was undetectable beforehand.
source: Both homozygous mutants lack the Reissner fiber and exhibit a typical curled-down phenotype, which arises from 28 to 30 hr post-fertilization (hpf) onwards and was undetectable beforehand (Cantaut-Belarif et al., 2018, Figure 1A, Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 1A and Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: urp2 gene expression shows a strong reduction in curled-down mutant embryos lacking the Reissner fiber compared to their control siblings.
source: Noticeably, we observed a strong reduction of urp2 gene expression in curled-down mutant embryos lacking the Reissner fiber compared to their control siblings (mean ± SEM fold decrease: 4.07 ± 1.2 in scospondinicm13/icm13 and 4.69 ± 1.77 in scospondinicm15/icm15, n = 3 replicates each, p-value<0.00005, GLM test; see Materials and methods and Figure 1—source data 2 for details).
evidence: This is demonstrated through RNA sequencing analysis with statistical significance.

claim: There was no significant decrease in urp1 transcript levels in scospondin mutants compared to control siblings.
source: There was no significant decrease in urp1 transcript levels (mean ± SEM fold decrease: 0.97 ± 0.06 in scospondinicm13/icm13 and 1.22 ± 0.25 in scospondinicm15/icm15, n = 3 replicates each, p-value=p = 0.191, GLM test).
evidence: This is demonstrated through RNA sequencing analysis with statistical significance.

claim: urp2 encodes for a secreted neuropeptide belonging to the Urotensin-II-related-peptide family.
source: The gene urp2 encodes for a secreted neuropeptide belonging to the Urotensin-II-related-peptide family (Tostivint et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Tostivint et al., 2014.

claim: urp1 and urp2 have been identified as both strongly downregulated in curled-down mutants.
source: Together with urp1, these transcripts have recently been identified as both strongly downregulated in curled-down mutants (Lu et al., 2020; Zhang et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Lu et al., 2020 and Zhang et al., 2018.

claim: urp1 expression level is not significantly decreased in scospondin homozygous mutants compared to their control siblings, neither at 30 hpf nor at 48 hpf.
source: Interestingly, we observed that urp1 expression level is not significantly decreased in scospondin homozygous mutants compared to their control siblings, neither at 30 hpf nor at 48 hpf (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is demonstrated through qRT-PCR analysis shown in Figure 1B.

claim: urp2 expression level shows a strong decrease at 48 hpf in scospondin mutant embryos compared to their control siblings.
source: Consistently with transcriptomic results, urp2 expression level shows a strong decrease at 48 hpf in mutant embryos compared to their control siblings (3.6 ± 0.2 fold decrease; mean ± SEM; Figure 1C).
evidence: This is demonstrated through qRT-PCR analysis shown in Figure 1C.

claim: urp2 expression level shows a strong decrease at 30 hpf in scospondin mutant embryos compared to their control siblings.
source: This is also true at the onset of the curled-down phenotype (30 hpf: 4.2 ± 0.5 fold decrease; mean ± SEM; Figure 1C) indicating that urp2 gene expression level is affected when embryos start to develop an abnormal morphogenesis of the posterior axis.
evidence: This is demonstrated through qRT-PCR analysis shown in Figure 1C.

claim: In zebrafish embryo the presence of the Reissner fiber in the CSF is required for the normal expression level of urp2, but not urp1.
source: Taken together, these data show that in zebrafish embryo the presence of the Reissner fiber in the CSF is required for the normal expression level of urp2, but not urp1.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the transcriptomic and qRT-PCR data showing differential effects on urp2 vs urp1.

claim: The expression of Urotensin-II-related peptides is restricted to the ventral population of CSF-cNs.
source: The expression of Urotensin-II-related peptides is restricted to the ventral population of CSF-cNs (Quan et al., 2015), known to exhibit spontaneous intracellular calcium variations around 30 hpf (Sternberg et al., 2018) when the curled-down phenotype becomes visible in scospondin mutants (Cantaut-Belarif et al., 2018 and Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Quan et al., 2015; Sternberg et al., 2018; Cantaut-Belarif et al., 2018.

claim: Ventral CSF-cNs exhibit spontaneous intracellular calcium variations around 30 hpf.
source: The expression of Urotensin-II-related peptides is restricted to the ventral population of CSF-cNs (Quan et al., 2015), known to exhibit spontaneous intracellular calcium variations around 30 hpf (Sternberg et al., 2018) when the curled-down phenotype becomes visible in scospondin mutants (Cantaut-Belarif et al., 2018 and Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Sternberg et al., 2018.

claim: Curled-down cilia-defective embryos lack early calcium transients in ventral CSF-cNs.
source: Curled-down cilia-defective embryos lack these early calcium transients (Sternberg et al., 2018) and do not form a proper Reissner fiber (Cantaut-Belarif et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Sternberg et al., 2018 and Cantaut-Belarif et al., 2018.

claim: Ventral CSF-cNs exhibit spontaneous calcium transients in wild-type embryos.
source: As previously described, we observed that ventral CSF-cNs exhibit spontaneous calcium transients in wild-type embryos (scospondin+/+, Figure 2B, Figure 2—video 1).
evidence: This is demonstrated through in vivo calcium imaging shown in Figure 2B.

claim: In heterozygous scospondinicm15/+ embryos, which display a straight body axis and form a proper Reissner fiber, ventral CSF-cNs retained the same level of activity as in wild-type.
source: Quantification of the integrated fluorescence variations over time showed that in heterozygous scospondinicm15/+ embryos, which display a straight body axis and form a proper Reissner fiber (Cantaut-Belarif et al., 2018), ventral CSF-cNs retained the same level of activity than in wild-type (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is demonstrated through quantification of calcium imaging data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Homozygous scospondinicm15/icm15 embryos exhibited a 52.8% decrease of calcium activity compared to wild-type.
source: On the contrary, homozygous scospondinicm15/icm15 embryos exhibited a 52.8% decrease of calcium activity compared to wild-type (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is demonstrated through quantification of calcium imaging data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: A reduction of 39% in calcium activity occurred in the null scospondinicm13/icm13 mutant compared to wild-type siblings.
source: A similar reduction of 39% occurred in the null scospondinicm13/icm13 mutant compared to wild-type siblings (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A,B).
evidence: This is demonstrated through quantification of calcium imaging data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A,B.

claim: The loss of the Reissner fiber reduces spontaneous calcium variations of ventral CSF-cNs during the critical time window for body axis straightening.
source: These data show that the loss of the Reissner fiber reduces spontaneous calcium variations of ventral CSF-cNs during the critical time window for body axis straightening.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the calcium imaging data showing reduced activity in scospondin mutants.

claim: The sparse spontaneous calcium transients in dorsal CSF-cNs were not affected by the absence of the Reissner fiber in both scospondin alleles.
source: On the contrary, the sparse spontaneous calcium transients in dorsal CSF-cNs were not affected by the absence of the Reissner fiber in both scospondin alleles (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C,D).
evidence: This is demonstrated through quantification of calcium imaging data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C,D.

claim: Early calcium transients in CSF-cNs require the non-selective cationic channels permeable Pkd2l1 channel in vivo.
source: Early calcium transients in CSF-cNs require the non-selective cationic channels permeable Pkd2l1 channel in vivo (Sternberg et al., 2018) that is permeable to calcium ions.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Sternberg et al., 2018.

claim: Pkd2l1 protein is enriched at the differentiating apical extension of CSF-cNs in curled-down scospondinicm15/icm15 mutants as well as in control embryos.
source: In toto immunohistochemistry for Pkd2l1 protein showed that this channel is enriched at the differentiating apical extension of CSF-cNs in curled-down scospondinicm15/icm15 mutants as well as in control embryos (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is demonstrated through immunohistochemistry shown in Figure 2D.

claim: In the absence of a Reissner fiber in scospondinicm15/icm15 mutants, spontaneous Pkd2l1 channel openings were similar to control embryos.
source: In order to assess Pkd2l1 channel properties, we performed in vivo whole-cell voltage-clamp recordings in double transgenic Tg(pkd2l1:GAL4;UAS:mCherry) embryos. In the absence of a Reissner fiber in scospondinicm15/icm15 mutants, we observed spontaneous Pkd2l1 channel openings that were similar to control embryos (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is demonstrated through in vivo voltage-clamp recordings shown in Figure 2E.

claim: The loss of the Reissner fiber decreases CSF-cNs intracellular calcium variations without preventing the opening nor the localization of Pkd2l1 channels in the differentiating apical extension of the cells.
source: Thus, the loss of the Reissner fiber decreases CSF-cNs intracellular calcium variations without preventing the opening nor the localization of Pkd2l1 channels in the differentiating apical extension of the cells.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the immunohistochemistry and electrophysiology data.

claim: The Reissner fiber is required for a signal acting on ventral CSF-cNs that controls both the spontaneous calcium variations and the expression of urp2 in the embryo.
source: Altogether, these data suggest that the Reissner fiber is required for a signal acting on ventral CSF-cNs that controls both the spontaneous calcium variations and the expression of urp2 in the embryo.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the combined calcium imaging and gene expression data.

claim: pkd2l1icm02/icm02 MZ mutant embryos did not display any defect in body axis morphogenesis and were morphologically indistinguishable from wild-type embryos.
source: We observed that pkd2l1icm02/icm02 MZ mutant embryos did not display any defect in body axis morphogenesis and were morphologically indistinguishable from wild-type embryos (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is demonstrated through morphological analysis shown in Figure 3B.

claim: pkd2l1icm02/icm02 mutants form a normal Reissner fiber in the central canal of the spinal cord at 30 hpf.
source: Using immunohistochemistry, we observed that pkd2l1icm02/icm02 mutants form a normal Reissner fiber in the central canal of the spinal cord at 30 hpf (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is demonstrated through immunohistochemistry shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Mutant pkd2l1icm02/icm02 clutches displayed a 4.9 fold decrease in pkd2l1 transcripts level compared to wild-type counterparts.
source: Indeed, mutant clutches displayed a 4.9 fold decrease in pkd2l1 transcripts level compared to wild-type counterparts (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is demonstrated through qRT-PCR analysis shown in Figure 3D.

claim: urp2 and urp1 gene expression were not decreased in pkd2l1icm02/icm02 embryos compared to wild-types.
source: Interestingly, we observed that urp2 and urp1 gene expression were not decreased in pkd2l1icm02/icm02 embryos compared to wild-types (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is demonstrated through qRT-PCR analysis shown in Figure 3D.

claim: The loss of Pkd2l1-driven calcium transients in CSF-cNs does not lead to a decreased expression of urp1 and urp2 transcripts.
source: Altogether, these data show that the loss of Pkd2l1-driven calcium transients in CSF-cNs does not lead to a decreased expression of urp1 and urp2 transcripts, rejecting the hypothesis of a direct requirement for urp2 expression of Pkd2l1-dependent intracellular calcium variations.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the qRT-PCR data in pkd2l1 mutants.

claim: There is a strict correlation between the presence of the Reissner fiber, a normal urp2 expression level and the proper morphogenesis of the embryonic body axis.
source: Instead, our results show a strict correlation between the presence of the Reissner fiber, a normal urp2 expression level and the proper morphogenesis of the embryonic body axis.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from comparing the phenotypes and gene expression in scospondin vs pkd2l1 mutants.

claim: The aberrant posterior axis curvature in absence of the Reissner fiber is a consequence of the decreased urp2 expression.
source: Altogether, our results prompted us to hypothesize that the aberrant posterior axis curvature in absence of the Reissner fiber is a consequence of the decreased urp2 expression.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on the correlation observed between Reissner fiber presence, urp2 expression, and body axis morphology.

claim: Embryos overexpressing urp2 showed much lower proportions of curled-down embryos compared to control injections.
source: In the four independent experiments conducted, injections with a control mRNA led to a proportion of curled-down embryos close to 25%, as expected (Figure 3F). On the contrary, embryos overexpressing urp2 showed much lower proportions of curled-down embryos (10.7 ± 1.5%; mean ± SEM; Figure 3F), suggesting that some homozygous mutants are rescued in this condition.
evidence: This is demonstrated through mRNA injection experiments and phenotype scoring shown in Figure 3F.

claim: urp2 overexpression led to detect straight or slightly curled-up scospondinicm15/icm15 embryos.
source: As expected, wild-type and heterozygous embryos injected with the control mRNA displayed a straight body axis, while scospondinicm15/icm15 showed a downward curvature of the posterior axis. Instead, urp2 overexpression lead to detect straight or slightly curled-up scospondinicm15/icm15 embryos at several instances (Figure 3E and G, Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is demonstrated through mRNA injection experiments, phenotype scoring, and genotyping shown in Figure 3E, G, and Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Restoring higher urp2 levels is sufficient to prevent the embryonic posterior axis defects in scospondin mutants.
source: Thus, restoring higher urp2 levels is sufficient to prevent the embryonic posterior axis defects in scospondin mutants.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the urp2 overexpression rescue experiments.

claim: urp2 neuropeptide expressed in CSF-cNs may signal at long-range to ensure a proper axis morphogenesis.
source: These observations confirm that urp2 neuropeptide expressed in CSF-cNs may signal at long-range, as suggested from the expression of the receptor in dorsal somites (Zhang et al., 2018), to ensure a proper axis morphogenesis.
evidence: This is inferred from the rescue experiments and supported by a citation to Zhang et al., 2018.

claim: Systemic bath applications of monoamines rescue body axis defects in curled-down cilia-defective mutants.
source: Recently, systemic bath applications of monoamines have been described to rescue body axis defects in curled-down cilia-defective mutants (Lu et al., 2020), (Zhang et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Lu et al., 2020 and Zhang et al., 2018.

claim: Epinephrine and norepinephrine have a moderate impact on the shape of the head-to-tail axis of initially straight embryos, which display a slight curled-up phenotype after exposure to monoamines.
source: Epinephrine and norepinephrine have a moderate impact on the shape of the head-to-tail axis of initially straight embryos, which display a slight curled-up phenotype after exposure to monoamines (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is demonstrated through monoamine treatment experiments and morphological analysis shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Control embryos exposed to a vehicle solution have an ear-to-tail angle distributed around 190.6° (median value).
source: This angle is distributed around 190.6° in control embryos exposed to a vehicle solution (median value; Figure 4C, bottom left graph).
evidence: This is demonstrated through quantification of ear-to-tail angles shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Control embryos exposed to monoamines exhibit a distribution of ear-to-tail angles shifted toward slightly higher values (median values: 220.4° and 213.6° for epinephrine and norepinephrine, respectively).
source: Comparatively, control embryos exposed to monoamines exhibit a distribution of ear-to-tail angles shifted toward slightly higher values (median values: 220.4° and 213.6° for epinephrine and norepinephrine, respectively; Figure 4C, bottom right graph).
evidence: This is demonstrated through quantification of ear-to-tail angles shown in Figure 4C.

claim: scospondinicm15/icm15 mutants treated with monoamines exhibit a reduction in the downward curvature of the posterior axis.
source: While mutant animals exposed to a vehicle solution display a typical curled-down body axis, scospondinicm15/icm15 mutants treated with monoamines exhibit a reduction in the downward curvature of the posterior axis (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is demonstrated through monoamine treatment experiments and morphological analysis shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Quantifications of ear-to-tail angles in scospondinicm15/icm15 mutants show a large increase of the median angle value after exposure to monoamines, compared to embryos treated with a vehicle solution (106.5° for vehicle, 167.1° for epinephrine and 158.5° for norepinephrine; median values).
source: Quantifications of ear-to-tail angles in scospondinicm15/icm15 mutants show a large increase of the median angle value after exposure to monoamines, compared to embryos treated with a vehicle solution (106.5° for vehicle, 167.1° for epinephrine and 158.5° for norepinephrine; median values; Figure 4C).
evidence: This is demonstrated through quantification of ear-to-tail angles shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Epinephrine and norepinephrine can partially restore the posterior axis geometry of scospondinicm15/icm15 mutants.
source: Altogether, these data show that epinephrine and norepinephrine can partially restore the posterior axis geometry of scospondinicm15/icm15 mutants, suggesting that monoamines can rescue the Reissner fiber-dependent signal required for a straight embryonic body axis.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the monoamine treatment experiments showing improved body axis angles.

claim: Monoamines can rescue the Reissner fiber-dependent signal required for a straight embryonic body axis.
source: Altogether, these data show that epinephrine and norepinephrine can partially restore the posterior axis geometry of scospondinicm15/icm15 mutants, suggesting that monoamines can rescue the Reissner fiber-dependent signal required for a straight embryonic body axis.
evidence: This is inferred from the ability of monoamines to rescue the body axis defects in scospondin mutants.

claim: In control siblings, urp1 expression remains comparable after vehicle, epinephrine or norepinephrine exposure.
source: In control siblings, urp1 expression remains comparable after vehicle, epinephrine or norepinephrine exposure (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is demonstrated through qRT-PCR analysis shown in Figure 4D.

claim: urp1 expression is not significantly modified in curled-down scospondinicm15/icm15 embryos compared to their control siblings receiving the same treatment.
source: Consistently with our previous results, urp1 expression is not significantly modified in curled-down scospondinicm15/icm15 embryos compared to their control siblings receiving the same treatment (1.01 ± 0.17-fold change; mean ± SEM; Figure 4D).
evidence: This is demonstrated through qRT-PCR analysis shown in Figure 4D.

claim: There is a slight increase of urp1 expression in curled-down mutant embryos treated with epinephrine and norepinephrine compared to vehicle treatment.
source: However, we observed a slight increase of urp1 expression in curled-down mutant embryos treated with epinephrine and norepinephrine compared to vehicle treatment (1.58 ± 0.43 and 1.28 ± 0.23 fold changes for epinephrine and norepinephrine respectively; mean ± SEM).
evidence: This is demonstrated through qRT-PCR analysis.

claim: urp2 expression level is significantly decreased in curled-down scospondinicm15/icm15 mutants compared to straight siblings.
source: As expected, urp2 expression level is significantly decreased in curled-down scospondinicm15/icm15 mutants compared to straight siblings (0.22 ± 0.06-fold change; mean ± SEM; Figure 4E).
evidence: This is demonstrated through qRT-PCR analysis shown in Figure 4E.

claim: Epinephrine and norepinephrine treatments do not change urp2 expression in control siblings.
source: Epinephrine and norepinephrine treatments also do not change urp2 expression in control siblings, but significantly increase it in curled-down homozygous mutant embryos (7.42 ± 4,23 and 4.67 ± 1.15 fold changes for epinephrine and norepinephrine respectively; mean ± SEM; Figure 4E).
evidence: This is demonstrated through qRT-PCR analysis shown in Figure 4E.

claim: Epinephrine and norepinephrine significantly increase urp2 expression in curled-down homozygous mutant embryos.
source: Epinephrine and norepinephrine treatments also do not change urp2 expression in control siblings, but significantly increase it in curled-down homozygous mutant embryos (7.42 ± 4,23 and 4.67 ± 1.15 fold changes for epinephrine and norepinephrine respectively; mean ± SEM; Figure 4E).
evidence: This is demonstrated through qRT-PCR analysis shown in Figure 4E.

claim: The rescue of the posterior axis curvature of scospondin homozygous mutant embryos by monoamines is associated with an increase of the expression of urp1 and urp2 neuropeptides.
source: These observations show that the rescue of the posterior axis curvature of scospondin homozygous mutant embryos by monoamines is associated with an increase of the expression of urp1 and urp2 neuropeptides.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the combined morphological and gene expression data after monoamine treatment.

claim: Epinephrine and norepinephrine compensate the loss of the Reissner fiber both on Urotensin-II-related neuropeptides expression and on posterior axis curvature.
source: Epinephrine and norepinephrine compensate the loss of the Reissner fiber both on Urotensin-II-related neuropeptides expression and on posterior axis curvature, suggesting that these compounds act on the Reissner fiber-dependent signaling pathway in the embryonic CSF.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the combined morphological and gene expression data after monoamine treatment.

claim: Monoamines act on the Reissner fiber-dependent signaling pathway in the embryonic CSF.
source: Epinephrine and norepinephrine compensate the loss of the Reissner fiber both on Urotensin-II-related neuropeptides expression and on posterior axis curvature, suggesting that these compounds act on the Reissner fiber-dependent signaling pathway in the embryonic CSF.
evidence: This is inferred from the ability of monoamines to rescue multiple aspects of the scospondin mutant phenotype.

claim: Norepinephrine diffuses down the central canal when injected in the hindbrain ventricle.
source: We observed an abundant norepinephrine-positive signal in the central canal of the rostral most region of the spinal cord 30 min post-injection, and the median and caudal most-regions 60 min post-injection, which was absent in control injections (Figure 5—figure supplement 1). This observation indicates that norepinephrine diffuses down the central canal when injected in the same conditions used for in vivo calcium imaging and that it is stable in the CSF after an hour, in agreement with former results in the mammalian ventricular system of dogs (Maas and Landis, 1965), sheeps (Forbes and Baile, 1974) and rats (Fuxe and Ungerstedt, 1966; Levitt et al., 1983).
evidence: This is demonstrated through immunostaining experiments shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1 and supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Norepinephrine is stable in the CSF after an hour.
source: We observed an abundant norepinephrine-positive signal in the central canal of the rostral most region of the spinal cord 30 min post-injection, and the median and caudal most-regions 60 min post-injection, which was absent in control injections (Figure 5—figure supplement 1). This observation indicates that norepinephrine diffuses down the central canal when injected in the same conditions used for in vivo calcium imaging and that it is stable in the CSF after an hour, in agreement with former results in the mammalian ventricular system of dogs (Maas and Landis, 1965), sheeps (Forbes and Baile, 1974) and rats (Fuxe and Ungerstedt, 1966; Levitt et al., 1983).
evidence: This is demonstrated through immunostaining experiments shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1 and supported by citations to prior work in mammals.

claim: An exogenous delivery of monoamines did not influence the basal calcium variations of ventral CSF-cNs in control embryos.
source: We first analyzed the effect of epinephrine and norepinephrine injections on control embryos displaying a straight body axis at 30 hpf and observed that an exogenous delivery of monoamines did not influence the basal calcium variations of ventral CSF-cNs (Figure 5B and D).
evidence: This is demonstrated through calcium imaging after monoamine injections shown in Figure 5B and D.

claim: Ventral CSF-cNs displayed a 44.1% decrease of calcium variations in scospondinicm15/icm15 embryos compared to control siblings in control condition with vehicle injections.
source: As described previously, ventral CSF-cNs displayed a 44.1% decrease of calcium variations in scospondinicm15/icm15 embryos compared to control siblings in control condition with vehicle injections (median value; Figure 5D and E), confirming the observations reported in Figure 3.
evidence: This is demonstrated through calcium imaging after vehicle injections shown in Figure 5D and E.

claim: Injections of epinephrine or norepinephrine in scospondinicm15/icm15 mutants increased the median ∫ΔF/F min−1 by 70.02 and 88.6%, respectively compared to vehicle injections.
source: Interestingly, injections of epinephrine or norepinephrine in scospondinicm15/icm15 mutants increased the median ∫ΔF/F min−1 by 70.02 and 88.6%, respectively compared to vehicle injections (Figure 5E).
evidence: This is demonstrated through calcium imaging after monoamine injections shown in Figure 5E.

claim: The rescue of the spontaneous activity of CSF-cNs by monoamines in mutant embryos reached comparable levels to those observed in control siblings.
source: Moreover, the rescue of the spontaneous activity of CSF-cNs by monoamines in mutant embryos reached comparable levels to those observed in control siblings (Figure 5D–E).
evidence: This is demonstrated through calcium imaging after monoamine injections shown in Figure 5D-E.

claim: Epinephrine and norepinephrine restore the Reissner fiber-dependent calcium transients in ventral CSF-cNs in scospondin mutants.
source: These data show that epinephrine and norepinephrine restore the Reissner fiber-dependent calcium transients in ventral CSF-cNs in scospondin mutants.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the calcium imaging data showing restored activity after monoamine injections.

claim: There exists a signal that links the Reissner fiber to both urp2 expression and calcium variations in ventral CSF-cNs that can be modulated by monoaminergic activation.
source: Altogether, our results are compatible with the existence of a signal that links the Reissner fiber to both urp2 expression and calcium variations in ventral CSF-cNs that can be modulated by monoaminergic activation.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the combined results showing monoamines can rescue both urp2 expression and calcium signaling.

claim: Endogenous epinephrine and norepinephrine may act locally to tune calcium signaling in CSF-cNs.
source: These observations suggest that endogenous epinephrine and norepinephrine may act locally to tune calcium signaling in CSF-cNs.
evidence: This is suggested based on the ability of exogenous monoamines to modulate calcium signaling.

claim: Norepinephrine positive puncta colocalized with the Reissner fiber as well as endogenous norepinephrine positive signals following patterns similar to extrafibrillar material labeled by the SCO-spondin-GFP fusion protein.
source: We observed norepinephrine positive puncta colocalized with the Reissner fiber as well as endogenous norepinephrine positive signals following patterns similar to extrafibrillar material labeled by the SCO-spondin-GFP fusion protein. This can also be observed closely at the level of the massa caudalis, formed by the accumulation of SCO-spondin at the caudal end of the central canal (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is demonstrated through immunostaining shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Norepinephrine is endogenously present in the embryonic CSF where it is associated with the Reissner-positive material in the central canal.
source: These observations suggest that norepinephrine is endogenously present in the embryonic CSF where it is associated with the Reissner-positive material in the central canal.
evidence: This is inferred from the immunostaining showing colocalization of norepinephrine with Reissner fiber material.

claim: Adrb2 is distributed ventrally in the neural tube, at the interface with the central canal, in a pattern that suggests a membrane localization in both control siblings and scospondinicm15/icm15 mutants.
source: We observed that Adrb2 is distributed ventrally in the neural tube, at the interface with the central canal, in a pattern that suggests a membrane localization in both control siblings and scospondinicm15/icm15 mutants (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is demonstrated through immunostaining shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Adrb2 localization is suitable for binding endogenous ligands present in the CSF.
source: Thus, Adrb2 localization is suitable for binding endogenous ligands present in the CSF.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that Adrb2 is localized at the interface with the CSF.

claim: The Adrb2 positive domain remains in the ventral midline, inserted between two rows of ventral CSF-contacting neurons.
source: Double immunostainings against Adrb2 and GFP in Tg(pkd2l1:GCaMP5G) control siblings show that both signals cover different domains in the ventral most region of the spinal cord (Figure 6C), where the Adrb2 positive domain remains in the ventral midline, inserted between two rows of ventral CSF-contacting neurons (Figure 6—video 1).
evidence: This is demonstrated through double immunostaining shown in Figure 6C and Figure 6—video 1.

claim: The medial cells expressing Adrb2 most probably correspond to the medial floor plate.
source: As ventral CSF-contacting neurons are known to derive from lateral floor plate progenitors (Park et al., 2004; Yang et al., 2010), the medial cells expressing Adrb2 most probably correspond to the medial floor plate.
evidence: This is inferred from the localization of Adrb2 and knowledge about CSF-cN developmental origins.

claim: The loss of calcium signaling in scospondinicm15/icm15 mutants is unlikely due to a defect in the Adrb2 distribution in the spinal cord.
source: Importantly, the same distribution is observed in scospondinicm15/icm15 mutants (Figure 6C and Figure 6—video 1). This observation suggests that the loss of calcium signaling in scospondinicm15/icm15 mutants is unlikely due to a defect in the Adrb2 distribution in the spinal cord.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that Adrb2 distribution is normal in scospondin mutants.

claim: Endogenous adrenergic signals could modulate the Reissner fiber-dependent signaling pathway that instructs body axis straightening during embryonic development.
source: Altogether, our results indicate that endogenous adrenergic signals could modulate the Reissner fiber-dependent signaling pathway that instructs body axis straightening during embryonic development, and suggests that monoamines act on CSF-contacting neurons through an indirect mechanism.
evidence: This is inferred from the combined results showing monoamine rescue, norepinephrine localization, and Adrb2 expression pattern.

claim: Monoamines act on CSF-contacting neurons through an indirect mechanism.
source: Altogether, our results indicate that endogenous adrenergic signals could modulate the Reissner fiber-dependent signaling pathway that instructs body axis straightening during embryonic development, and suggests that monoamines act on CSF-contacting neurons through an indirect mechanism.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that Adrb2 is not expressed in CSF-cNs but in adjacent floor plate cells.

claim: The Reissner fiber is essential for signaling to the developing CSF-contacting neurons.
source: Using a combination of transcriptomic analyses together with in vivo calcium imaging and pharmacology, we show here that the Reissner fiber is essential for signaling to the developing CSF-contacting neurons (CSF-cNs).
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the combined results of transcriptomic, calcium imaging, and pharmacological experiments.

claim: In CSF-cNs, the Reissner fiber is required for both urp2 expression and spontaneous intracellular calcium variations.
source: In these neurons, the Reissner fiber is required for both urp2 expression and spontaneous intracellular calcium variations.
evidence: This is demonstrated through transcriptomic analysis and calcium imaging showing both are reduced in scospondin mutants.

claim: The functional interaction between the Reissner fiber and ventral CSF-cNs is required for a normal curvature of the developing posterior axis of zebrafish.
source: This functional interaction between the Reissner fiber and ventral CSF-cNs is required for a normal curvature of the developing posterior axis of zebrafish.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that loss of the Reissner fiber affects both CSF-cN function and body axis morphology.

claim: The CSF-cNs response to the signal from the Reissner fiber can be modulated by local adrenergic activation in vivo.
source: Using monoamine injections into the CSF, we show that the CSF-cNs response to the signal from the Reissner fiber can be modulated by local adrenergic activation in vivo, suggesting that the Reissner fiber acts by controlling the availability of a chemical signal in the CSF.
evidence: This is demonstrated through monoamine injection experiments showing rescue of calcium signaling and body axis defects.

claim: The Reissner fiber acts by controlling the availability of a chemical signal in the CSF.
source: Using monoamine injections into the CSF, we show that the CSF-cNs response to the signal from the Reissner fiber can be modulated by local adrenergic activation in vivo, suggesting that the Reissner fiber acts by controlling the availability of a chemical signal in the CSF.
evidence: This is suggested based on the ability of monoamines to substitute for the Reissner fiber and the detection of norepinephrine associated with the fiber.

claim: urp2 may not be the only determinant of embryonic axis morphogenesis downstream of the Reissner fiber.
source: However, urp2 may not be the only determinant of embryonic axis morphogenesis downstream of the Reissner fiber, as single urp2 morpholino knockdown does not show a defective axis curvature (Zhang et al., 2018).
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that urp2 knockdown alone does not phenocopy the scospondin mutant, supported by a citation to Zhang et al., 2018.

claim: Parallel signaling pathways that would likely act post-transcriptionally may be involved in axis morphogenesis downstream of the Reissner fiber.
source: Parallel signaling pathways that would likely act post-transcriptionally and would therefore not be detected using our transcriptomic strategy may be involved.
evidence: This is speculated based on the limited number of genes identified in the transcriptomic analysis.

claim: A newly generated scospondin hypomorphic allele revealed urp2 as the major downregulated gene in homozygous mutant and did not report a urp1 downregulation.
source: In line with our results, the investigation of a newly generated scospondin hypomorphic allele (Rose et al., 2020) also revealed urp2 as the major downregulated gene in homozygous mutant and did not report a urp1 downregulation.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Rose et al., 2020.

claim: A newly generated scospondin hypomorphic allele revealed an inflammatory signature induced by the loss of the Reissner fiber at the embryonic stage.
source: The discovery of a new hypomorphic allele for scospondin recently revealed an inflammatory signature induced by the loss of the Reissner fiber at the embryonic stage (Rose et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Rose et al., 2020.

claim: The authors did not detect an inflammatory signature in their transcriptomic analysis.
source: In our work, we did not detect such a signature in our transcriptomic analysis (see Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the text and refers to Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Embryonic CSF-cNs are not fully differentiated, as they do not harbor a fully developed apical extension known to tune their mechanosensory function at larval stage.
source: However, embryonic CSF-cNs are not fully differentiated, as they do not harbor a fully developed apical extension known to tune their mechanosensory function at larval stage (Desban et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Desban et al., 2019.

claim: The Reissner fiber acts via the modulation of the CSF content.
source: We therefore favor the hypothesis that the Reissner fiber acts via the modulation of the CSF content, which is supported by the restoration of calcium signaling in CSF-cNs upon monoamine injections in the brain ventricles.
evidence: This is inferred from the ability of monoamine injections to rescue calcium signaling.

claim: One possible interpretation is that the Reissner fiber is essential for the control of endogenous epinephrine and norepinephrine distribution in the embryonic CSF.
source: One possible interpretation of our results is that the Reissner fiber is essential for the control of endogenous epinephrine and norepinephrine distribution in the embryonic CSF.
evidence: This is speculated based on the ability of monoamines to rescue the phenotype and the detection of norepinephrine associated with the fiber.

claim: There are noradrenergic neurons in the embryonic hindbrain as early as 24 hpf.
source: This is consistent with our immunodetection of norepinephrine in close vicinity with the Reissner fiber in the embryonic central canal. This hypothesis is supported by the presence of noradrenergic neurons in the embryonic hindbrain as early as 24 hpf (Holzschuh et al., 2003), providing a potential source of monoamines that would need to be transported caudally to the central canal of the spinal cord.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Holzschuh et al., 2003.

claim: Adrb2 belongs to the G protein-coupled receptors family and was identified to trigger cytoplasmic calcium raise in vitro.
source: Interestingly Adrb2 belongs to the G protein-coupled receptors family and was identified to trigger cytoplasmic calcium raise in vitro (Galaz-Montoya et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Galaz-Montoya et al., 2017.

claim: In zebrafish, the adrenergic system plays important roles in the control of wakefulness and of cardiac contractions.
source: In zebrafish, the adrenergic system plays important roles in the control of wakefulness (Singh et al., 2015) and of cardiac contractions (Steele et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Singh et al., 2015 and Steele et al., 2011.

claim: No morphological defects have been reported in animals missing the rate-limiting enzyme for the synthesis of epinephrine and norepinephrine.
source: However, no morphological defects have been reported in animal missing the rate-limiting enzyme for the synthesis of epinephrine and norepinephrine (Singh et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Singh et al., 2015.

claim: The cross-talk between the Reissner fiber and undifferentiated CSF-cNs is likely to be of chemical nature, possibly through monoamines themselves.
source: Nonetheless, our results support the idea that the cross-talk between the Reissner fiber and undifferentiated CSF-cNs is likely to be of chemical nature, possibly through monoamines themselves.
evidence: This is inferred from the combined results showing monoamine rescue and norepinephrine association with the fiber.

claim: Monoamines act on CSF-cNs in an indirect manner.
source: They further support the idea that monoamines act on CSF-cNs in an indirect manner.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that Adrb2 is not expressed in CSF-cNs.

claim: A temporally controlled inactivation of cilia motility leads to spine curves reminiscent of adolescent idiopathic scoliosis.
source: Interestingly, a temporally controlled inactivation of cilia motility leads to spine curves reminiscent of adolescent idiopathic scoliosis (Grimes et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Grimes et al., 2016.

claim: The Reissner fiber and Urp reception in slow muscles are implicated in the maintenance of a straight spine during postembryonic development.
source: Recent results suggest that, as in the embryo, the Reissner fiber and Urp reception in slow muscles are also implicated in the maintenance of a straight spine during postembryonic development (Lu et al., 2020; Rose et al., 2020; Troutwine et al., 2020; Zhang et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Lu et al., 2020; Rose et al., 2020; Troutwine et al., 2020; Zhang et al., 2018.
